data.text: The Majuli case study aims to provide an immersive VR tour of the island's ecological and cultural heritage. The application contains extensive multimodal content including images, videos, and 3D models totaling almost 10 gigabytes. Because rendering this content requires a computational requirement many times higher than rendering a simple static image, resource optimization is necessary because regular systems cannot support the application.
points: The Majuli case study aims to provide an immersive VR tour of the island's ecological and cultural heritage.
The application contains extensive, geographically spread information points with two levels of content.
The tour uses a multimodal archive of images, videos, and 3D models totaling almost 10 gigabytes.
Rendering this content requires a computational requirement many times higher than rendering a simple static image.
Resource optimization is necessary because regular systems cannot support the Majuli application.

data.text: The Oculus Quest 2 is a standalone device with its own processor and memory. Because it has less computing power and storage than a high-end workstation, the application required optimization to reduce size and computational demands. By storing videos in the cloud and loading them on demand, the application size was reduced to 5.1 GB. However, this optimization relies on high bandwidth, network coverage, and low latency to load high-quality content in real time.
points: The Oculus Quest 2 is a standalone device with its own processor and memory.
The Quest 2 requires optimization because it has less computing power and storage than a high-end workstation.
Cloud-based optimization stores videos in the cloud and loads them on demand to reduce local storage and data-access requirements.
This optimization reduced the application size to 5.1 GB and decreased computational requirements.
Cloud-based optimization requires high bandwidth, network coverage, and low latency to load high-quality videos in real time.

data.text: Cardboard headsets provide a low-cost option for VR on smartphones, but the full Majuli VR system exceeds the capabilities of average smartphones. Optimization techniques like image compression and removing video playback can significantly reduce system size, although these trade-offs make the experience less realistic. If a device cannot perform the rendering, developers may need to use cloud-based services or remove features entirely.
points: Cardboard headsets provide a low-cost option for VR on smartphones.
The Majuli VR system exceeds the computation and storage capabilities of average smartphones.
Optimization techniques like image compression and removing video playback can significantly reduce system size.
These trade-offs make the VR experience less realistic than the full version.
If a device cannot perform the rendering, developers may use cloud-based services or remove features.

data.text: The book Computer Graphics published by Oxford University Press is the source for the topics covered and can be used for further study. The NPTEL MOOC on computer graphics covers all of these topics and the stages of the three-dimensional graphics pipeline.
